# Adaptive b-bit OPH containment benchmark contract

**Note:** This file was generated by ChatGPT 5.6 Sol under the direction of Adam Phillippy.

> **Historical artifact:** This records pre-hardening design evidence and does not define the current production method. See `docs/SCIENTIFIC_SPEC.md` and ADR 0004.

Schema version: `backend-v2`

This contract is frozen before the adaptive benchmark is run. Results may not be
removed because they are unfavorable. Changes to fixtures, reference scores, timing
boundaries, parameter sweeps, or acceptance gates require a new schema version.

## Candidate under test

The candidate retains the direct, undensified, bit-sliced b-bit OPH backend from
`backend-v1`, using ntHash2, 14 comparison bits, 32-bit winner verification, and HLL
precision 12. Minmers are not used.

For a directed comparison of core set `A` with expanded set `B`, the candidate first
estimates how many aligned OPH winners would be expected at the useful display floor:

```text
C_floor = 0.80^k
I_floor = C_floor * |A|
U_floor = |A| + |B| - I_floor
J_floor = I_floor / U_floor
occupied_union_registers = R * (1 - exp(-U_floor / R))
expected_matches = occupied_union_registers * J_floor
```

Cardinalities come from the existing HLL summaries, except that an available exact
sparse-core cardinality replaces the HLL numerator cardinality. If
`expected_matches` is below the configured threshold and the core's complete distinct
canonical-hash set fits within the configured cap, that directed containment is
computed exactly. Otherwise it remains the OPH/HLL estimate. The two directed scores
are combined using the existing maximum-containment rule. Display identity remains
`ANI = C^(1/k)`.

Exact sparse-core hashes are collected directly from the k-mer stream; they are not a
second sketch or a sample of the OPH sketch. A core is discarded from the exact
channel as soon as its distinct cardinality exceeds the cap. Opposite-axis matches
are found with a query-only postings map and one half-bin scan, then deduplicated
before exact containment and direction are calculated.

## Frozen sweep

The selection sweep uses ntHash2 and the Balanced tier of 1,024 OPH registers:

* sparse distinct-k-mer caps: 512, 1,024, 2,048, 4,096, 8,192, and 16,384;
* minimum expected matches: 8, 12, 16, and 24;
* useful display floor: exact `C^(1/k) >= 0.80`.

After selection, the winning adaptive configuration is checked at 512, 1,024, 2,048,
and 4,096 registers. A tier is exposed only if it independently passes.

## Fixtures and references

All 15 `backend-v1` deterministic fixtures and every matrix cell remain required. The
primary reference is the exact maximum directed containment of complete distinct
canonical k-mer sets. MashMap-compatible coordinated bottom-s remains a secondary
sanity check only.

The CHM13 chromosome 1 higher-order alpha-satellite sample is the required real-data
accuracy and repeat-context check. Full chromosome 1 is used only for final browser
runtime and memory validation after a configuration passes the native correctness
gate; constructing an all-k-mer exact oracle for a whole chromosome is out of scope.

## Acceptance gates

For every fixture:

* false-missing cells: zero;
* false-present cells: zero;
* expected forward/reverse diagonal cells: no direction inversions;
* among cells whose exact display identity is at least 0.80:
  * mean absolute containment error: at most 0.010;
  * 95th-percentile absolute containment error: at most 0.030;
  * maximum absolute containment error: at most 0.080;
  * mean absolute displayed-ANI error: at most 0.010;
  * 95th-percentile absolute displayed-ANI error: at most 0.025;
  * maximum absolute displayed-ANI error: at most 0.050.

Cells below 0.80 are retained in the report but do not determine acceptance. This is
intentional: at `k=21`, mutation survival makes k-mer-derived ANI unstable in that
range even when containment itself is exact.

## Timing and selection

Build time includes normal OPH/HLL axis construction and bounded sparse-core
retention. Matrix time includes OPH comparison, the query-only opposite-axis scan,
exact sparse intersections, and score selection. Reports include the retained sparse
core count, retained exact hashes, adaptive directed comparisons, first-view total
time, and estimated owned bytes.

Correctness is mandatory. Among configurations passing every fixture, selection is
lexicographic: smallest exact-cardinality cap, then smallest expected-match threshold,
then lowest median first-view time. This deliberately minimizes worst-case browser
memory and the number of corrected comparisons before considering small timing
differences.
